subject: Catalyst Bank — LLM data use: derivative protections, prompt custody, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@catalystbank.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ciso@catalystbank.com
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: LLM data use / no-training requirement + evidence pack request

David —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a handful of specific asks before we can move the pilot forward:

- A contractual no-adaptive-training (no-train) commitment for customer data AND derived prompts/responses; we need explicit language that customer-provided prompts and model outputs will not be used to improve your public or internal models.
- Clarification of prompt/response IP and whether our transcripts/outputs will be considered customer property or subject to any derivative licensing.
- Full subprocessors list (hosted & third-party inference, analytics, monitoring) and confirmation of onshore processing for EU-resident datasets.
- Evidence: KMS key attestations, SOC 2 section references, and an example log export showing pseudonymized telemetry we can expect for audit.

I've attached our questionnaire (one PDF). Can you confirm timeline to provide redlines and an ops evidence pack? Our procurement window is tight — we'd like a mutual action plan this week if possible.

Warmly,
Lina Ortega
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Catalyst Bank

Lina —

Thanks for the checklist and the clear asks. We can meet each of these but want to be explicit about mechanics and evidence. Proposed next steps:

1) Legal redlines: I'll loop in Kimberly (cc) to propose DPA language that includes a binding no-adaptive-training clause and explicit output/prompt ownership grant to Catalyst. Expect a redline by EOD today.
2) Ops evidence: Jordan and Neha (cc) will assemble a short evidence pack (KMS key IDs, SOC 2 control references, sanitized sample log export) and a playbook for onshore routing. Target: tomorrow COB.
3) Subprocessors: we'll provide a current inventory plus our gating controls for adding new subprocessors and an SLA for advance notice.

Can you confirm the residency requirement scope: is it strictly EU member states for data at rest/processing, or do you also require onshore keys (KMS) and audit logs in EU? That determines whether we can meet with our standard hosted offering or if we need dedicated private deployment.

If it's helpful, here's a short shared checklist/drive where we'll drop artifacts: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2catalyst-llm-evidence

Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: LLM data use / no-training requirement + evidence pack request

Hi Lina —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is an initial DPA redline focused on three principle changes you requested:

- No-adaptive-training clause: we accept an explicit prohibition on using customer prompts and outputs to improve our models used in production or research; we will also include an operational definition of "model improvement" to avoid ambiguity (training, fine-tuning, gradient aggregation).
- Prompt/response ownership: proposed clause grants Catalyst ownership of prompts and outputs and a perpetual, exclusive-ish license back to Redwood only for providing the contracted inference service (not for model training).
- Subprocessor and onshore routing: added a section requiring 30-day notice before adding subprocessors that process Catalyst data and commitment to route EU-resident data to EU-hosted compute (or Dedicated/Private deployment if required).

Operational evidence we will supply (tomorrow):
- KMS key material and Key IDs used when onshore routing is enabled.
- SOC 2 controls map (CC1–CC8 references) and auditor contact info under NDA.
- Example log export (sanitized) that demonstrates telemetry we keep and how it is pseudonymized in transit.

One sensitivity to call out: our hosted multi-tenant offering uses aggregated telemetry to monitor system health. We can provide sampling and pseudonymization proofs, but a strict prohibition on any telemetry that could be considered a signal for model improvement will likely push the deployment toward a Dedicated or Private model. We flagged that in the redline and included fallback language for an operational review.

Please review the attached redline and let us know the non-negotiables for Catalyst so we can finalize an MOP (mutual action plan).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: LLM data use / no-training requirement + evidence pack request

Kimberly, David —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear redline. A few clarifications from Catalyst Security:

- The word "exclusive-ish" in the license language isn't acceptable; we need unambiguous customer ownership of prompts and outputs and a narrow license to Redwood solely to provide the service and for debugging/operational purposes with strict deletion windows. Please remove any language that permits derivative training.
- Residency: we require both EU-hosted processing and EU-resident KMS for the trial data. If Redwood cannot guarantee KMS residency for the pilot, Catalyst will require Dedicated capacity in EU region.
- Evidence: the SOC 2 control map + sanitized log export look good in principle, but we need an auditor contact and a sample of the raw export schema (column names) so our GRC tooling can validate.

Next steps: we will review your redline and propose our redlines by Friday. We also want to schedule a short call with Jordan and Neha to validate the log schema and routing architecture. Available windows: Thu 09:00–11:00 or Fri 14:00–16:00 CEST.

Appreciate the responsiveness — this is the level of detail our procurement team needs to clear internal signoff.

Best regards,
Lina Ortega
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Catalyst Bank
